candidate_relations.reason: VCA IgM positivity, CSF EBV DNA, lymphocytic pleocytosis, seizures, and leptomeningeal enhancement establish EBV meningoencephalitis.
Enteroviral meningitis is a different virus; CSF contains EBV DNA with a positive VCA IgM.
Normal CSF glucose and protein, low procalcitonin, and 80% lymphocytes conflict with typical bacterial meningitis.

candidate_relations.reason: Eastern equine encephalitis is not supported; the serologic and CSF evidence is primary EBV.
Seizures and altered consciousness indicate acute encephalitis but omit EBV and the meningeal CSF/imaging findings.
SSPE is a delayed measles process in older children, not acute tonsillitis with VCA IgM and CSF EBV DNA.
La Crosse encephalitis has no supporting exposure or serology, unlike documented EBV in blood and CSF.
EBV encephalitis captures seizures and cortical infarcts but omits CSF pleocytosis and leptomeningeal enhancement that complete meningoencephalitis.
West Nile virus meningitis is a flavivirus illness; the confirmed pathogen here is EBV.
Circumferential brainstem T2 rims with leptomeningeal enhancement and CSF EBV DNA favor infectious meningoencephalitis over ADEM.
Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis similarly does not fit a two-day febrile pharyngitis with absent EBNA and CSF EBV DNA.
Viral meningoencephalitis is the parent syndrome and does not specify Epstein–Barr virus.
Viral meningitis accounts for stiff neck and CSF lymphocytes but not seizures, unresponsiveness, or cortical infarcts.
VCA IgM-positive infectious mononucleosis is the systemic EBV illness and omits meningoencephalitis.
Meningoencephalitis names the CNS pattern but not the EBV etiology proven in CSF.
A one-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure is a manifestation of the encephalitis, not the etiologic diagnosis.
EBV encephalitis again fits the parenchymal disease and still leaves out the meningitic CSF 250 cells and sulcal enhancement.
Viral encephalitis is a broader parent missing both EBV and concomitant meningitis.
Parietal cortical infarcts are complications of the EBV meningoencephalitis rather than a primary cerebral vasculitis.
Epstein-Barr virus meningoencephalitis is the same diagnosis supported by CSF EBV DNA plus mixed meningeal and parenchymal injury.
